arxiv-1910-06682.title: Hydra: A Multiple Blockchain Protocol for Improving Transaction Throughput
arxiv-1910-06682.creator: Rowel Gündlach, Jaap-Henk Hoepman, Remco van der Hofstad, Tommy Koens, Stijn Meijer
arxiv-1910-06682.description: Abstract Improving transaction throughput is one of the main challenges in decentralized payment systems. Attempts to improve transaction throughput in cryptocurrencies are usually a trade-off between throughput and security or introduce a central component. We propose Hydra, a decentralized protocol that improves transaction throughput without the security trade-off and has no central component.

arxiv-2002-09093.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Linear Models for Visual Foresight in Object Pile Manipulation
arxiv-2002-09093.creator: H.J. Terry Suh 1, Russ Tedrake 1
arxiv-2002-09093.description: Abstract In this paper, we tackle the problem of pushing piles of small objects into a desired target set using visual feedback. Unlike conventional single-object manipulation pipelines, which estimate the state of the system parametrized by pose, the underlying physical state of this system is difficult to observe from images.

arxiv-2007-06642.title: The magnetic obliquity of accreting T Tauri stars 2020 The magnetic obliquity of accreting T Tauri stars – 5
arxiv-2007-06642.creator: Pauline McGinnis, Jérôme Bouvier, Florian Gallet
arxiv-2007-06642.description: Abstract Classical T Tauri stars (CTTS) accrete material from their discs through their magnetospheres. The geometry of the accretion flow strongly depends on the magnetic obliquity, i.e., the angle between the rotational and magnetic axes. We aim at deriving the distribution of magnetic obliquities in a sample of 10 CTTSs.

arxiv-2102-02448.title: Safety during Transient Response in Direct Current Microgrids using Control Barrier Functions
arxiv-2102-02448.creator: K. C. Kosaraju, S. Sivaranjani, V. Gupta
arxiv-2102-02448.description: Abstract We consider the problem of guaranteeing that the transient voltages and currents stay within prescribed bounds in Direct Current (DC) microgrids, when the controller does not have access to accurate system dynamics due to the load being unknown and/or time-varying. To achieve this, we propose an optimization based controller design using control barrier functions.

arxiv-2110-08959.title: Fast and Exact Outlier Detection in Metric Spaces: A Proximity Graph-based Approach DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Conference: SIGMOD ’21: ACM SIGMOD International Conference of Management of Data; June 21–26, 2021; Xi’an, Shaanxi, China SIGMOD ’21: ACM SIGMOD International Conference of Management of
arxiv-2110-08959.creator: Daichi Amagata, Makoto Onizuka, Takahiro Hara
arxiv-2110-08959.description: Abstract . Distance-based outlier detection is widely adopted in many fields, e.g., data mining and machine learning, because it is unsupervised, can be employed in a generic metric space, and does not have any assumptions of data distributions. Data mining and machine learning applications face a challenge of dealing with large datasets, which requires efficient distance-based outlier detection algorithms.

arxiv-2112-08481.title: Maximum likelihood estimation for randomized shortest paths with trajectory data
arxiv-2112-08481.creator:
ame Ilkka Kivimäki ∗ 
ame Bram Van Moorter, Manuela Panzacchi 
ame Jari Saramäki, 
ame Marco Saerens
arxiv-2112-08481.description: Abstract Randomized shortest paths (RSP) are a tool developed in recent years for different graph and network analysis applications, such as modelling movement or flow in networks. In essence, the RSP framework considers the temperature-dependent Gibbs-Boltzmann distribution over paths in the network.

arxiv-2210-01443.title: Analysis of the rate of convergence of an over-parametrized
arxiv-2210-01443.creator: deep neural network estimate learned by gradient descent
arxiv-2210-01443.description: Abstract September 1, 2022 Abstract Estimation of a regression function from independent and identically distributed random variables is considered. The L_{2} error with integration with respect to the design measure is used as an error criterion. Over-parametrized deep neural network estimates are defined where all the weights are learned by the gradient descent.

arxiv-2302-10456.title: Investigating the effects of Lorentz Invariance Violation on the CP–sensitivities of the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment
arxiv-2302-10456.creator: Arnab Sarker, Abinash Medhi, Moon Moon Devi
arxiv-2302-10456.description: Abstract The neutrino oscillations offer great potential for probing new-physics effects beyond the Standard Model. Any additional effect on neutrino oscillations can help understand the nature of these non-standard effects. The violation of fundamental symmetries may appear as new-physics effects in various neutrino experiments.

arxiv-2306-16722.title: Evaluating Paraphrastic Robustness in Textual Entailment Models
arxiv-2306-16722.creator: Dhruv Verma, Yash Kumar Lal, Shreyashee Sinha, Benjamin Van Durme, Adam Poliak
arxiv-2306-16722.description: Abstract We present P ^ ​ a ​ R ​ T ​ E \hat{P}aRTE , a collection of 1,126 pairs of Recognizing Textual Entailment (RTE) examples to evaluate whether models are robust to paraphrasing. We posit that if RTE models understand language, their predictions should be consistent across inputs that share the same meaning.

arxiv-2310-12644.title: THE DAMPED FOCUSING CUBIC WAVE EQUATION ON A BOUNDED DOMAIN
arxiv-2310-12644.creator: Thomas Perrin
arxiv-2310-12644.description: Abstract Abstract. For the focusing cubic wave (or Klein-Gordon) equation on a compact Riemannian manifold of dimension 3 , the dichotomy between global existence and blow-up for solutions starting below the energy of the ground state is known since the work of Payne and Sattinger.

arxiv-2311-17167.title: Comparing SCUBA-2 and ALMA Selections of Faint DSFGs in Abell 2744 Facilities: ALMA, JCMT astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2022 )
arxiv-2311-17167.creator: S. J. McKay, A. J. Barger, L. L. Cowie
arxiv-2311-17167.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by S. J. McKay, A. J. Barger, L. L. Cowie. We make a comparison of deep SCUBA-2 450 μ \mu m and 850 μ \mu m imaging on the massive lensing cluster field Abell 2744 with Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) 1.2 mm data. Our primary goal is to assess how effective the wider-field SCUBA-2 sample, in combination with red JWST priors, is for finding faint dusty star-forming galaxies (DSFGs) compared to the much more expensive mosaicked ALMA observations.

arxiv-2408-10152.title: Source-Seeking Problem with Robot Swarms
arxiv-2408-10152.creator: Antonio Acuaviva, Hector Garcia de Marina, Juan Jimenez
arxiv-2408-10152.description: Abstract We present an algorithm to solve the problem of locating the source, or maxima, of a scalar field using a robot swarm. We demonstrate how the robot swarm determines its direction of movement to approach the source using only field intensity measurements taken by each robot.

arxiv-2408-11160.title: Statistical Challenges with Dataset Construction: Why You Will Never Have Enough Images
arxiv-2408-11160.creator: Josh Goldman, John K. Tsotsos
arxiv-2408-11160.description: Abstract Deep neural networks have achieved impressive performance on many computer vision benchmarks in recent years. However, can we be confident that impressive performance on benchmarks will translate to strong performance in real-world environments? Many environments in the real world are safety critical, and even slight model failures can be catastrophic.

pmc-10669334.title: The Effect of Roll Circular Vection on Roll Tilt Postural Responses and Roll Subjective Postural Horizontal of Healthy Normal Subjects
pmc-10669334.creator: Taylor W Cleworth, John H J Allum, Emma I Nielsen, Mark G Carpenter, Peter Federolf
pmc-10669334.description: Background: Falls and related injuries are critical issues in several disease states, as well as aging, especially when interactions between vestibular and visual sensory inputs are involved. Slow support surface tilt (0.6 deg/s) followed by subjective postural horizontal (SPH) assessments have been proposed as a viable method for assessing otolith contributions to balance control.

pmc-11362892.title: Old, the new, more or less and the conundrum for biomarkers in cardiovascular diseases?
pmc-11362892.creator: Pupalan Iyngkaran
pmc-11362892.description: Biomarkers are critical for diagnostic, monitoring and management of cardiovascular diseases. Opportunities to improve how biomarkers are used are important. This editorial on biomarkers in coronary artery disease provides commentary on the study as well as broad benchmarks on what make ideal biomarkers. Biomarker discovery is difficult and opportunities to expand and improve their use should be encouraged.

pmc-11472337.title: PEDOT:PSS Wire: A Two-Terminal Synaptic Device for Operation in Electrolyte and Saline Solutions
pmc-11472337.creator: Seiya Watanabe, Hiroaki Shibakita, Naruki Hagiwara, Ryosuke Nakajima, Hiroyuki S. Kato, Megumi Akai-Kasaya
pmc-11472337.description: Synaptic devices, which are designed to emulate the synaptic functions of neurons, have recently gained attention as key elements in the development of neuromorphic hardware. To date, most synaptic devices utilizing conductive polymer materials, particularly poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS), have been designed as three-terminal devices.

pmc-11505268.title: Current Applications of Raman Spectroscopy in Intraoperative Neurosurgery
pmc-11505268.creator: Daniel Rivera, Tirone Young, Akhil Rao, Jack Y. Zhang, Cole Brown, Lily Huo, Tyree Williams, Benjamin Rodriguez, Alexander J. Schupper
pmc-11505268.description: Background: Neurosurgery demands exceptional precision due to the brain’s complex and delicate structures, necessitating precise targeting of pathological targets. Achieving optimal outcomes depends on the surgeon’s ability to accurately differentiate between healthy and pathological tissues during operations. Raman spectroscopy (RS) has emerged as a promising innovation, offering real-time, in vivo non-invasive biochemical tissue characterization.

pmc-11506939.title: Inhibition of Biogenic Amines in Fermented Tilapia Surimi by Collaborative Fermentation of Latilactobacillus sakei and Pediococcus acidilactici
pmc-11506939.creator: Chunsheng Li, Chunhui Wang, Jianchao Deng, Di Wang, Hui Huang, Yongqiang Zhao, Shengjun Chen, Andrea Gomez-Zavaglia
pmc-11506939.description: Fermentation is an effective method for ameliorating the gelation properties of freshwater fish surimi, but the formation of biogenic amines (BAs) during fermentation should also be controlled. In this study, the BAs in fermented tilapia surimi were inhibited by the collaborative fermentation of Latilactobacillus sakei and Pediococcus acidilactici, followed by the revelation of the BA inhibition mechanism.

pmc-12530788.title: Transradial catheterization for prone neurosurgical treatment in a hybrid operating room: Technical considerations
pmc-12530788.creator: Taichi Ikedo, Masakazu Okawa, Hideo Chihara, Hiroyuki Ikeda, Shigeki Takada, Takeshi Funaki, Takayuki Kikuchi, Chiaki Sakai, Yoshiki Arakawa
pmc-12530788.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Surgical management of cerebrovascular diseases in a hybrid operating room (HOR) is advantageous in patients requiring postoperative cerebral angiography to confirm complete obliteration or in procedures requiring a combined open and endovascular approach. However, in the prone position, conventional transfemoral arterial access is challenging, as the introducer sheath is positioned between the patient and the surgical table, impeding catheter maneuverability.

pmc-12731521.title: Beyond the Exome: The Role of Noncoding and Regulatory Variants in Monogenic Diseases
pmc-12731521.creator: Efthalia Moustakli, Nektaria Zagorianakou, Stylianos Makrydimas, Andreas Miltiadous, Alexandros T Tzallas, George Makrydimas, Grzegorz Wegrzyn
pmc-12731521.description: Analysis of coding areas has long been used to study monogenic illnesses, but despite the extensive use of whole-exome sequencing (WES), up to half of suspected cases remain genetically unexplained. Variants outside coding areas can alter splicing, transcript stability, or gene regulation, compromising normal gene activity.

pmc-13271794.title: Utility of genomic sequencing classifier in managing cytologically indeterminate oncocytic thyroid nodules
pmc-13271794.creator: Sara Ahmadi, Anupam Kotwal, Athanasios Bikas, Benjamin F Altshuler, Anery Patel, Gunjan Arora, Elena G Hughes, Jetesh Sahadeo, Michael W Yeh, Masha J Livhits
pmc-13271794.description: ContextOncocytic cells can occur in benign and malignant thyroid nodules, posing a diagnostic challenge. This has reduced the diagnostic performance of molecular testing for indeterminate oncocytic thyroid nodules.ObjectiveTo evaluate the performance of Afirma genomic sequencing classifier (GSC) in thyroid nodules with Bethesda III or IV cytology and oncocytic predominance.
